title: Eventual flatness of coefficient subalgebra inclusions
statement: Let k be a field, Λ an Artinian local k-algebra with residue field K, σ:K→Λ a section of reduction, and t a finite subset of Λ whose ideal span is its maximal ideal. Let c be a finite subset of K such that the image of k in Λ lies in the subring generated by t and σ(k(c)). There is a finite subset d of K such that, for every finite s containing both d and c, the inclusion C_s→Λ of [def-weil-pbc-artinian-coefficient-subalgebra] is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. No local-ring or finiteness conclusion about C_s is asserted.

source.place: Tag 07FG, proof of lemma-helper, polynomial images and final presentation paragraph

proof.text: Evaluate the polynomial ring K[t] using the section sigma. Its image contains t and sigma(K). For the inclusion of its image S in Lambda, the contraction J of the maximal ideal has extension equal to the maximal ideal, since t generates it. Both ideals are nilpotent. The private module_complete_of_nilpotent helper proves adic completeness for every module over a commutative ring with a nilpotent ideal: vanishing of I^N times the module forces every Cauchy sequence to be constant after N and gives Hausdorffness. Specializing this general statement to the two rings gives their adic completeness. The section gives surjectivity modulo J, and Mathlib surjective_of_mk_map_comp_surjective gives surjectivity onto Lambda. These are proved private helpers, not unproved dependencies.

By Hilbert basis the kernel has a finite set G of generators. Take d to be the union of their finite coefficient sets. For s containing d, each generator is in the image of F[t] to K[t], F=k(s), by MvPolynomial.mem_range_map_iff_coeffs_subset. It follows by Ideal.span_le and Ideal.mem_map_of_mem that the kernel of the restricted evaluation extends to the full evaluation kernel.

The polynomial coefficient map F[t] to K[t] is flat: its tensor presentation identifies it with extension of the field map F to K. Quotient base change therefore makes the induced map modulo the restricted kernel flat. The first isomorphism theorem identifies the source quotient with the restricted evaluation image and the target quotient with Lambda, using the proved surjectivity. Compose these ring equivalences with the flat quotient map. No separate proof of injectivity by faithfully flat ideal contraction is needed.

Polynomial induction shows the evaluation image equals the subring closure of t and sigma(F). Since c is contained in s, monotonicity of intermediate-field adjoin and the hypothesis hc show this closure contains the image of k. Algebra.adjoin_eq_ring_closure then identifies it with the coefficient subalgebra. Rewrite the inclusion flatness along this equality.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_artinian_coefficient_eventual_flatness
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (Λ : Type v) [CommRing Λ] [Algebra k Λ]
    [IsArtinianRing Λ] [IsLocalRing Λ]
    (σ : IsLocalRing.ResidueField Λ →+* Λ) (t : Finset Λ)
    (c : Finset (IsLocalRing.ResidueField Λ))
    (hσ : (IsLocalRing.residue Λ).comp σ = RingHom.id _)
    (ht : Ideal.span (t : Set Λ) = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal Λ)
    (hc : ∀ a : k, algebraMap k Λ a ∈ Subring.closure ((t : Set Λ) ∪
      σ '' (IntermediateField.adjoin k (c : Set (IsLocalRing.ResidueField Λ)) :
        Set (IsLocalRing.ResidueField Λ)))) :
    ∃ d : Finset (IsLocalRing.ResidueField Λ),
      ∀ s : Finset (IsLocalRing.ResidueField Λ), d ⊆ s → c ⊆ s →
        RingHom.Flat (artinianCoefficientSubalgebra k Λ σ t s).val.toRingHom
